proxyError.title: Polaris Proxy Error
proxyError.body: The proxy has stopped. Open Polaris for details.

proxyMisdirected.title: Polaris traffic not routed as expected
proxyMisdirected.body: The proxy is still running, but traffic may not be going through it (possible unencrypted direct connection). Open Polaris for details.

systemDnsTakeoverFailed.title: Polaris DNS takeover degraded
systemDnsTakeoverFailed.body: Linux system DNS could not be connected to Polaris. The proxy is still running, but DNS may fail or bypass DNS rules. Check Helper and systemd-resolved, then reconnect.

ruleResourcesMissing.title: Polaris routing rules degraded
ruleResourcesMissing.body: Some rule resources have no local copy, so the routing rules referencing them were skipped. Download them on the Rule Resources page and reconnect to restore.

outboundInterfaceUnavailable.title: Polaris outbound interface unavailable
outboundInterfaceUnavailable.body: The selected outbound interface is missing or inactive. This connection was not applied to prevent switching to another interface. Open Polaris and choose an available interface.

tsLogin.title: Tailscale Sign-in
tsLogin.body: Your browser was opened to complete Tailscale sign-in.

fakeIpTun.title: TUN Mode
fakeIpTun.body: FakeIP was enabled automatically for TUN mode (recommended). You can turn it off in Settings → DNS.

helperNotInstalled.title: Polaris could not start TUN mode
helperNotInstalled.body: TUN mode requires the privileged helper, but it couldn't be installed. Open the app and go to Settings › Helper to install it, then try again

tunRouteNotCaptured.title: Polaris could not capture the default route
tunRouteNotCaptured.body: Another VPN is holding the default route, so Polaris couldn't capture traffic. Disconnect the other VPN and try again.

rootOrphanBlocked.title: Polaris core startup blocked
rootOrphanBlocked.body: A leftover process is holding the cache file. Open Polaris for details.

autoSwitchNeedsRestart.title: Polaris could not switch nodes automatically
autoSwitchNeedsRestart.body: The current node is unreachable, and some candidate nodes need the core restarted before they can take over. Open Polaris to switch nodes manually.

tunAdapterMissing.title: Polaris could not create the TUN adapter
tunAdapterMissing.body: sing-box started, but the TUN adapter never appeared, so traffic was not captured. Check whether security software is blocking the wintun driver, then restart and try again.

settings.listImportHint: One entry per line or comma-separated; duplicates are skipped

general.silentStartDesc: Starts without showing the main window, straight to the system tray
general.autoLightweightModeDesc: Release the interface after it has been hidden or minimized for 10 minutes; the tray and proxy keep running
general.keepTrayMenuWarmDesc: Enabled by default. Preloads the tray menu after app startup and keeps it ready while hidden, independently of main-window lightweight mode; this typically uses about 30–40 MB more memory. When disabled, it is created on demand and released after 2 minutes hidden.
general.desktopNotificationsDesc: Raises a system notification when the proxy hits a serious error
general.autoPrivacyModeDesc: After 10 idle minutes the window locks behind a password so nobody can read over your shoulder; the proxy keeps running
general.privacyPasswordPlaceholder: Leave empty to clear the password
general.autoConnectDesc: Restore the last exit node and takeover mode, then connect
general.autoCheckUpdateDesc: Notify when a new version is found
general.rememberWindowSizeDesc: Restore the last window layout the next time you open it
general.hardwareAccelerationDesc: Turning this off switches to software rendering, which can fix a blank window, visual artifacts, or a repeatedly crashing GPU process on some devices. Restart Polaris to take effect.
general.windowEffectsDescMac: Frosted glass on macOS. Turning this off uses a solid background, which can fix a blank window or compositing glitches. Restart Polaris to take effect.
general.windowEffectsDescWin: Mica material on Windows. Turning this off uses a solid background, which can fix a blank window or compositing glitches. Restart Polaris to take effect.

coreVersion.noBackupDesc: Core version changed to {{currentVersion}}. No backup is available for rollback.
coreVersion.rollbackSuccess: Rollback successful — reopen the app to apply the previous core
coreVersion.rollbackConfirmDesc: This rolls back to {{version}}; the core will restart.
coreVersion.sameVersionGoManage: Please confirm the same-version replacement in the Core Management card.
coreVersion.baselineOverrideGoManage: The selected core is older than the bundled baseline; confirm the temporary replacement in the Core Management card.
coreVersion.noRollbackEntryNote: No backup is available to roll back to: the core update pipeline is not wired up yet, so no backup is produced.

coreManagement.crossBandFound: A new cross-band version {{version}} was found and will not be auto-updated; to upgrade, check manually or update with the app.
coreManagement.crossBandRisk: Crosses a major version — higher risk; review before updating
coreManagement.upToDate: The core is already up to date
coreManagement.checkTimeout: Checking for core updates timed out (over {{sec}}s). Please try again later.
coreManagement.autoUpdateNoSchedulerHint: When on: the core is checked for updates once a day in the background. A new version is staged first and only applied while the proxy is stopped, so your connection is never interrupted. Major-version jumps are only reported, never applied automatically.
coreManagement.channelDesc: Stable considers only GitHub stable releases; Testing also takes alpha / beta / rc. Crossing a minor version is still limited by the next option
coreManagement.channelPrereleaseNote: Current channel: Testing (includes alpha / beta / rc)

restartApp.title: Restart Polaris to apply
restartApp.message: These settings are saved, but they only take effect after Polaris restarts: {{items}}.
restartApp.persistNote: Choosing “Later” discards nothing — the change is already written to your config file. This session keeps running with the old value, and the new one applies the next time Polaris starts.
restartApp.proxyNote: “Restart now” stops the proxy core first, so the current connection drops; after the restart it comes back according to your “Connect on startup” setting.

network.enableIPv6Desc: Enables system-wide IPv6 resolution and routing. If the exit node has no IPv6, connections that go over IPv6 hang until they time out.
network.ipv6NodeFakeIpHint: If the node lacks IPv6, some sites may be unreachable; enabling FakeIP is recommended.
network.speedTestUrlDesc: Target URL requested for speed testing (default generate_204).
network.meshLoginFallback: Fall back to direct during mesh login
network.meshLoginFallbackDesc: While the chosen Tailscale exit is not connected, login and authorization go direct so the auth page cannot deadlock
network.refreshDashboardDone: Panel asset cache cleared — the core will re-download it the next time it starts
network.dashboardNotRunning: Panel unavailable — enable the management panel and connect the proxy first
network.directInterfaceDesc: Bind sing-box direct traffic and direct DNS to a physical interface.
network.proxyInterfaceDesc: Physical interface used when a proxy node has no local override.
network.interfaceListFailed: Could not read network interfaces; the current setting was preserved
network.bypassHint: Domains and CIDRs that skip the system proxy.
network.sharedListBold: This is the same list as TUN · Excluded subnets
network.blockQuicDescFull: Rejects UDP 443 towards proxy nodes so browsers fall back to TCP through the proxy, keeping QUIC from slipping past routing or leaking
network.webrtcLeakDesc: Off / forward STUN through the proxy / reject STUN outright. Only takes effect in TUN mode
network.webrtcTunOnlyNote: Only takes effect in TUN mode — switch the takeover mode to TUN on the home screen to use it
network.interruptOnSwitch: Drop old connections on node switch
network.interruptOnSwitchDesc: On by default: switching nodes drops the old connections. Off means a graceful switch — existing connections stay until they close on their own
network.restartOnNodeChangeDesc: When on, all node changes apply automatically and restart the proxy only when needed. When off, unused-node changes wait for manual apply; nodes in use are still handled automatically.
network.mgmtEnable: Enable the management API and built-in dashboard
network.mgmtEnableDesc: Off by default. Exposes the sing-box control API on 127.0.0.1 for the built-in dashboard
network.mgmtPortDesc: Assigned automatically by default; you can pin it
network.mgmtSecretDesc: Generated automatically and checked when the dashboard loads
network.officialDashboardDesc: Open the sing-box dashboard in Polaris; it connects automatically while the core is running

proxyMode.confirmDesc: Switching the takeover mode restarts the proxy to apply it, briefly dropping the current connection.
proxyMode.fakeIpAutoEnabled: FakeIP was enabled automatically for TUN mode (recommended). You can turn it off in Settings → DNS.

advanced.dnsInvalid: Unrecognized DNS address (supports https:// DoH, tls:// DoT, udp:// or IP); not saved, please correct
advanced.fakeIpTunOffConfirmDesc: In TUN mode, after disabling, proxy nodes will receive real IPs instead of domains. Some airports with strict anti-abuse policies may refuse the connection (invalid certificate or block page), and this risk cannot be mitigated by the client. Overseas first-connection latency will also increase. Disable anyway?
advanced.fakeIpFilterDesc: These domains use real DNS instead of a fake IP. Recommended on.
advanced.optimisticCacheDesc: On expiry, return the stale answer first and refresh in the background. Lowers tail latency.
advanced.dnsTimeoutDesc: Per-query timeout in ms. Empty uses the core default. Keeps slow upstreams from stalling resolution.
advanced.coreBaselineWarnDesc: Non-official core {{current}} is below the bundled baseline {{bundled}}; it may be incompatible with the new config (connection failures / missing features). Upgrade the core manually, or reset to the bundled official core in Settings · Core.
advanced.mainSessionViaProxyDesc: Route app/core update checks and rule downloads through the proxy.
advanced.bypassLANDesc: Ranges/domains in the list go direct, not through the proxy. Turn off to let them use the proxy.
advanced.tlsFragmentDesc: Splits the ClientHello for every TLS node to resist SNI-based DPI
advanced.tipSessionOnly: Terminal proxy settings are only effective in the current session
advanced.tipPermanent: For permanent settings, add the command to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc
advanced.tipDisable: To disable proxy: delete or comment out the relevant environment variables
advanced.autoSwitchNodeDesc: Switches to a working node automatically when the current one is detected as faulty. Intranet-only mesh nodes are excluded: nothing can substitute for them, so they are never switched away.
advanced.disableLogFileDescFull: Stops sing-box logging. Live logs and log-based diagnostics become unavailable; crash detection is unaffected. While connected, save first and apply when ready; while stopped, it takes effect on the next connection.
advanced.neighborDomainsHint: One suffix per line (leading dot added automatically); dot-less short names under it (e.g. nas.lan) resolve via LAN devices.
advanced.neighborDomainInvalid: Invalid suffix in the list; those entries will not take effect.
advanced.macFilterDesc: Limit or exclude which LAN devices' traffic enters the TUN (by MAC).
advanced.macFilterHint: One MAC per line (00:11:22:33:44:55); requires auto_route, Linux only.
advanced.macInvalid: Invalid MAC in the list (use 00:11:22:33:44:55); those entries are dropped when generating the config.
advanced.nodeResolverSingleHint: Single upstream, no concurrent fault-tolerance (falls back to a single DNS).
advanced.bypassLANOffNote: The "Bypass LAN" master switch is off, so excluded ranges have no effect (the kernel-side exclusion list is empty). To restore it, enable the switch under Network · System Proxy.

about.openExternalFail: Could not open the external link
about.uninstallDesc: Removes the launch-at-login entry, the privileged helper, the core in the protected directory, all user configuration (subscriptions, nodes, rules, logs), downloaded update packages, the app preferences domain (macOS: the in-app language setting), and the app itself. Requires clicking the button twice and cannot be undone.
about.uninstallStepHelper: Uninstall privileged helper (incl. core in protected directory)
about.uninstallVerdictIncomplete: Partly done — manual steps still required
about.uninstallExitHint: Configuration or the application itself has been deleted. Please quit Polaris.
about.tagline: Every connection, always pointed the right way
about.intro: Polaris is a modern sing-box-based proxy client, built to keep proxy control and connection management simple.
about.noTelemetry: Zero telemetry — no crash reports, no analytics, nothing sent back

update.formMismatch: The update package does not match the current install form; handed to the system
update.portableManualReplace: The portable update was downloaded to: {{path}}. Quit Polaris, then extract the archive over your current program folder to finish updating. The portable build has no installer — do not double-click to install.

macosGatekeeper.title: About the macOS security prompt
macosGatekeeper.message:
This app uses ad-hoc signing (no paid Apple Developer certificate). The installer script automatically clears the download quarantine attribute, so the update normally opens fine.

If you still see "unidentified developer", open Finder → Applications, right-click Polaris → choose Open → click Open again in the dialog. It will launch normally from then on.

windowsSmartScreen.title: About the Windows security prompt
windowsSmartScreen.message:
This app has no Authenticode code-signing certificate, so Windows SmartScreen may show "Windows protected your PC / Unknown publisher".

This cannot be suppressed from inside the app. When it appears, click "More info", then "Run anyway" to continue installing.

debElevation.title: Administrator authorization required
debElevation.message:
Installing the .deb update requires system privileges. After you click Continue, the app exits and the system shows a PolicyKit dialog asking for your password.

If you cancel that dialog, nothing is updated and you can retry later.

update.autoDownloadAppDesc: When on: if a new version is found at startup, the installer is downloaded in the background. It is never installed automatically — you decide when to restart and install.
update.bannerDesc: Open Settings → Updates to read the release notes and install it.
update.autoDownloadAppDescOff: Only checks and notifies; does not auto-download.
update.pageSub: Updates for the app, the core and rule resources, plus download acceleration
update.intervalCardSub: Subscriptions and rule resources refresh in the background on this cycle; app updates are checked once at every startup
update.ghAccelSub: Optional. Applies to GitHub downloads of the app, the core and rule resources
update.ghNote: The original address is always tried first; the accelerator domain is used only when one is set and the original request fails
update.appChannelDesc: Stable considers only GitHub stable releases; Testing also includes alpha / beta / rc. Startup, tray and manual checks all follow this setting.
update.prereleaseNote: An alpha / beta / rc build that may contain unfixed issues. It is considered only when the Testing channel is selected.
update.reinstallCurrentTip: Only re-downloads and verifies the current installer; it will not replace the app until you confirm installation afterward.
update.reinstallUnavailable: The latest release in this channel does not match the installed version, or has no suitable package. Nothing was downloaded, avoiding an unintended downgrade.
update.digestMissingBefore: This release ships no sha256 digest, so the downloaded installer cannot be matched byte for byte against the publisher. Updating is not blocked; if a GitHub accelerator mirror is enabled, that mirror is inside the trust boundary for this download.
update.digestMissingAfter: This download was not checked against a sha256 digest — the release ships none, so the installer cannot be confirmed byte for byte against the publisher. Whether to install is your call.

err.missingDownloadUrl: Update info is missing the download URL (internal error; retry or download manually)
err.digestFieldInvalid: The release digest field is malformed (publisher issue; retrying will not help)
err.cacheDirFailed: Failed to create the update cache directory
err.downloadFailed: Failed to download the update package
err.sizeMismatch: Package size does not match the release manifest (possibly truncated or tampered)
err.digestHexInvalid: The release sha256 digest is not valid hex (publisher issue; retrying will not help)
err.digestMismatch: Package verification failed (possibly truncated or tampered)
err.landingFailed: Failed to finalize the downloaded package on disk

update.coreCardSub: A staged update is only applied while the core is stopped
update.coreCardSub2: Core downloads follow the GitHub acceleration setting above as well
update.coreStagedDesc: Applies the next time the core stops
update.restrictMinor: Auto-update only within a compatible minor version
update.restrictMinorDesc: Crossing a minor version can change behaviour, so auto-update skips it. On by default
update.subAutoStartupOnly: Checks for catch-up when Polaris starts. The background check interval is set to Manual only, so there is no scheduled refresh.
update.subAutoWithInterval: Checks for catch-up when Polaris starts, then follows the background check interval.
update.subPerSubNote: A subscription refreshes automatically only when both this global switch and its own Auto Update switch are on.
update.subChannelDesc: Follow each subscription's own setting, force everything through the proxy, or force everything direct
update.ruleResourceAutoDesc: Re-downloads rule resources on the background check interval

backup.pageSub: Export and import by category. Works with Polaris backup files
backup.catDnsResources: DNS servers, server groups, and resolution defaults

tun.pageSub: Virtual adapter, network stack and excluded subnets
tun.stackDesc: Pick the tunnel stack; per-platform behaviour and advice are below
tun.autoRouteDesc: Opens routes for LAN and mesh traffic per platform; the mechanics are below
tun.strictRouteDesc: Locks all traffic into the TUN so nothing leaks around it; may break direct LAN access and VM networking — turn it off first when something cannot connect
tun.natTypeDesc: Defaults to full cone; stricter modes reduce UDP and P2P hole-punching success.
tun.detStackMixed: TCP goes through System, UDP through gVisor. Its TCP half collapses at large MTU just like System.
tun.detStackGvisor: Fully user-space. The only stack that can take a large MTU; measured fastest on Windows.
tun.detStackSystem: Kernel stack, the lowest overhead. But on Windows it collapses badly at large MTU.
tun.detStackAuto: Follows the per-platform recommendation below; the MTU default follows it too.
tun.detStackMac: gVisor recommended — the kernel utun gets shaky under load, and user space avoids the reverse-route packet loss of the network extension.
tun.detStackWin: gVisor recommended — measured on one machine: gVisor with a large MTU comes close to the no-tunnel ceiling, while System under the same conditions keeps only about one percent of it.
tun.detStackLinux: System recommended — native kernel routing has the lowest overhead, and no measurable throughput difference between stacks was found.
tun.detRouteWin: Excludes private subnets as a whole to avoid a gateway-lookup loop, then punches a hole for the routes of each enabled mesh (WireGuard/Tailscale).
tun.detRouteMac: Never excludes the physical LAN subnet — doing so triggers reverse-route packet loss in the system network extension and pages hang.
tun.detRouteLinux: The exclusion list is meaningless at kernel level and can even hurt (it splits the routing table and breaks same-subnet direct access), so it is ignored — no need to fill it in.
tun.routeExcludeHint: These subnets bypass the TUN and route directly (LAN, corporate intranet, and so on).
tun.sharedListBold: This is the same list as Network · Bypass list
tun.sharedListRest: (this page only takes its CIDR entries); editing either place changes both.
tun.inboundExcludeHint: When something reaches this machine back through a mesh or NAT, requests coming from these subnets bypass the TUN
tun.inboundLinuxNote: On Linux the kernel policy routing already protects server replies, so this has no effect (it is ignored)
tun.mtuDesc: Leave empty for automatic, derived from the stack and the platform. Fill it in only when tuning by hand.
tun.mtuInvalid: MTU must be a whole number between {{min}} and {{max}}

dns.pageSub: System takeover, query runtime, and node resolution
dns.bootstrapIpOnly: Bootstrap DNS must use system DNS or an IP address endpoint
dns.bootstrapDirectOnly: Bootstrap DNS must query through the direct outbound
dns.builtinRequired: Built-in servers provide default and bootstrap resolution and must remain enabled
dns.serverPortInvalid: Port must be an integer from 1 to 65535
dns.hostsPaths: Hosts file paths, comma-separated; leave empty for the system default
dns.groupRaceDesc: Query all members concurrently; the first successful response wins
dns.groupFallbackDesc: Try members one by one in the order shown below
dns.groupRaceDegraded: Fewer than two race members are available; this currently behaves as one server
dns.groupMembersRequired: Add at least one member server
dns.groupNoMembers: No servers added; this group cannot produce a DNS response
dns.connectionResolutionHint: Passing the hostname lets the egress handle it when supported. Local resolution runs the complete DNS rule chain, skips FakeIP actions while obtaining a real address, and stops the connection if resolution fails.
dns.resourceInUse: Cannot delete: resource is in use
dns.fakeIpDesc: Answers with fake IPs to dodge DNS poisoning
dns.bootstrapDesc: When a remote or domestic DNS address uses a hostname, resolve it through these IP-based DoH services instead of the local DNS.
dns.bootstrapNone: The current DNS servers use IP addresses; no preliminary lookup is needed
dns.takeoverSystemDnsDesc: Restores the original system DNS automatically after a crash or power loss
dns.raceStrategyDesc: Queries several upstreams at once and takes the first complete answer back
dns.raceUpstreamsDesc: Save any number of custom upstreams; enable up to 3 built-in and custom upstreams in the race. System DNS is a fallback tier and does not count against the quota
dns.raceQuotaReached: 3/3 enabled; disable one racing upstream first
dns.saveCustomFirst: Enter and save this upstream before enabling it
dns.customDohIpOnly: Must be a bare IP form (e.g. 223.5.5.5 or tls://223.5.5.5:853); domain names are rejected
dns.raceEmptyFallback: With everything off, it falls back to the default ali/dnspod race
dns.fakeIpFilterHint: These domains resolve to real IPs (NTP time sync, STUN, captive-portal checks, and the like)
dns.browserDohDesc: A browser's built-in Secure DNS bypasses this app's DNS handling, so domain routing and FakeIP don't apply to it. When on, endpoints on the list are rejected on 443/853 and QUIC, forcing the browser back to system DNS. Off by default.
dns.browserDohHint: Matched by domain suffix (cloudflare-dns.com covers all its subdomains). The built-in entries are a starting point, not a complete list — a DoH endpoint can be any self-hosted domain, so add whatever you find missing.

dnsWorkspace.defaultLast: Runs after no custom rule matches
dnsWorkspace.systemRuleNode: Node and endpoint domains: use real DNS to avoid dial loops
dnsWorkspace.systemRuleBootstrap: DNS server domains: resolve through the explicit Bootstrap server

field.echHint: Encrypts the ClientHello and hides the SNI (anti-censorship).
field.h2HeadersHint: One "Name: value" per line; repeated names are merged.
field.h2HostHint: Comma-separated; empty falls back to the SNI / node address.
field.hostKey: Host public key (comma-separated; empty accepts any)
field.http3Hint: Uses QUIC transport instead of TCP.
field.httpTlsHint: Connects to the proxy over HTTPS.
field.hy2NetworkHint: Restricts which network types this node carries; empty = no restriction (both TCP and UDP).
field.isEndpoint: Treat as an endpoint (not an outbound)
field.isEndpointHint: Tick this for endpoint-type protocols of third-party cores (e.g. a custom WireGuard implementation).
field.muxHint: Carries several proxy connections over one underlying connection, cutting handshake overhead.
field.muxPadHint: Adds random padding to multiplexed streams to strengthen fingerprint resistance. Off = the key is not written at all (the core default is off too).
field.noParrotHint: Since sing-box 1.14, Hysteria2 parrots Chrome's QUIC handshake by default. Chrome does not declare Ed25519 support, so a server whose certificate is Ed25519 always fails the handshake. Turn this on if the node never connects.
field.reuseHint: Reuses the underlying connection (v2 CONNECT) to cut handshake overhead.
field.spoofMethodHint: Sends a decoy ClientHello before the real handshake. Requires elevated privileges, is unsupported on ARM64, and needs a domain different from the real SNI.
field.stlsHint: Layers ShadowTLS camouflage on top of Shadowsocks.
field.tlsEngineHint: Uses the OS-native TLS stack so the ClientHello fingerprint looks genuine. It only takes effect on the matching platform; the wrong choice is simply not written to the config.
field.tlsFragmentHint: Splits the TLS ClientHello to bypass SNI-based blocking. Try it only when the handshake is reset; it adds latency and some servers may reject it. Not available for Hysteria2, TUIC, or NaiveProxy.
field.zeroRttHint: Saves one round trip but weakens replay protection (off by default in the core).
field.torArgsHint: Space-separated, passed through to the tor process
field.meshRoutesHint: One subnet per line for forced routing through this node. Leave empty to disable forced subnet routing. OpenConnect/OpenVPN routes arrive after connection and cannot be filled automatically.
field.insecureCryptoHint: Only for legacy gateways; lowers transport security
field.sysIfaceHint: Routing is taken over by the core; the node then carries traffic on its own and changes require a core restart
field.ovpnCaHint: Required. The core refuses to start without TLS material
field.redirectGwHint: Points the default route at this VPN; equivalent to WireGuard allowed_ips 0.0.0.0/0
field.ovpnTlsExtraJsonHint: Written only into the tls object, for example peer_fingerprint or server_name. Keep protocol-level extensions separate.
field.extraJsonHint: Fields not listed above, written as a JSON object using sing-box key names; merged verbatim into the config on save. Controls above win on name collision. Leave empty for none.
field.torrcHint: Native torrc syntax, one `Key Value` per line (e.g. `ExitNodes {jp}`). Blank lines and # comments are not saved — the core side is a key/value map and cannot hold them.
